facts.complete_units: SaveData_Value whole Value and register/compile definitions
facts.meaning: Registration validates symbol/block, constructs the complete Value first, and appends it. Duplicate IDs remain multiple registrations; compile loops in registration order, so every save callback runs and the later same-ID result overwrites the hash slot. unregister removes every matching registration.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: A failing constructor is not appended. A later save callback/validation failure prevents later callbacks and prevents save_to_file opening output; earlier callback side effects are not restored. Dynamic extra registration order remains external.

facts.meaning: A registration class check is Object.const_get(class_symbol) then is_a?, not nested object-graph validation. Save and load validate each object; load marks loaded only after its callback returns. valid?(hash) checks every registration including missing-key nil, whereas load_values uses a present key, otherwise its new-game proc when defined.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: No all-values preflight is performed by load_values. A later failure can leave earlier globals assigned and loaded flags true. Missing without new-game proc is skipped. A callback that mutates then raises is not marked loaded but its external mutation can remain. Unknown hash keys are not loaded by these loops.

facts.meaning: Default17 registration order is player, frame_count, game_system, pokemon_system, switches, variables, self_switches, game_screen, map_factory, game_player, global_metadata, map_metadata, bag, storage_system, essentials_version, game_version, stats. Exactly game_system, pokemon_system, essentials_version, game_version and stats are boot-loaded. Only stats is reset_on_new_game. map_factory has no new-game proc.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: This is the fixed built-in registration set before plugin overrides/additions; it is not the engine object-graph inventory. Constructor failures stop the sequential new-game/boot loop at their actual prefix.

facts.meaning: player saves/loads the Player object through $player; Player inherits Trainer party and initializes a Pokedex field. storage_system saves/loads $PokemonStorage as PokemonStorage. global_metadata uses $PokemonGlobal/PokemonGlobalMetadata, map_metadata uses $PokemonMap/PokemonMapMetadata, and bag uses $bag/PokemonBag. Party and Pokedex are not separate built-in top-level SaveData IDs.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: This local code passes complete top-level objects to Marshal rather than manually projecting Pokemon fields. Pokemon/Pokedex/PokemonStorage inner instance-variable schemas, alias/cycle behavior, plugins, and exact binary payloads are not received by this contribution.

facts.meaning: File reader takes the first Marshal object as-is if it is a Hash; otherwise it reads sequential objects into an array until EOF, then adapter uses each registration old-format selector and omits nil. read_from_file runs conversion only for nonempty adapted data and rewrites the same requested path in wb only if conversions return true. save_to_file builds the hash before opening its output in wb.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: There is no file transaction or rollback in these methods; a serialization failure after open can retain truncation/partial bytes. Class/inner-field validation is performed by later Value APIs, not by accepting the first Hash. All old creature conversions are a separate contribution.

facts.meaning: Boot chooses initialize_bootup_values versus load_bootup_values by adapted hash emptiness. start_new loads eligible new-game registrations, samples uptime, increments sessions, then creates the map factory and refreshes encounter/map state. Game.load loads eligible registrations first, then samples uptime/increments sessions, then loads/updates map and only finally assigns Scene_Map.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: A failed later map stage can leave player/storage/global assignments, loaded marks and session increment intact. New-game factory is established outside the map_factory registration because it has no new-game proc. Complete map/transfer/event runtime remains OPEN.

facts.meaning: Normal save validates arguments, writes safesave, increments save_count, writes magic number and samples stats last-saved time before compile/write. Only IOError and SystemCallError cause save_count decrement and false return.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: Type/InvalidValueError/other exceptions escape; prior safesave, magic/time writes are not generally undone. On handled file errors only save_count is decremented, not the entire state. A successful return proves only that local calls returned, not every inner creature field or later reload.

facts.meaning: Event.trigger passes positional arguments only when callback arity is greater than two and equals provided count; otherwise it passes first sender argument plus an array of remaining arguments. trigger2 always spreads supplied arguments. Duplicate + callbacks are suppressed by include?; set clears then adds one.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: Callback exception aborts later callbacks with earlier side effects retained; there is no transaction, cancel flag or rescue in these primitive definitions. This dispatch family must not be confused with NamedEvent.

facts.meaning: EventHandlers.add lazily creates a NamedEvent and assigns named callback; same key replaces that value. trigger looks up the actual event name and spreads caller arguments into each callback in stored hash order. Unknown event returns nil; remove/clear of absent event are safe navigation no-ops.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: No sender or argument array is automatically injected. A caller giving a Pokemon object hands that object directly; callback mutation is visible to subsequent subscribers and to caller. Exception stops later subscribers; all concrete producers/subscribers still need separate reception.

facts.meaning: Symbol-handler lookup converts a non-Symbol responding to id, tries an exact truthy handler first, then condition handlers in insertion order. trigger passes the normalized symbol as the first callback argument. remove deletes exact entry only; clear clears exact and conditional stores. copy resolves current source lookup then stores that same handler for destination keys.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: A removed exact key may still match a conditional handler. Handler reference is shared rather than deep copied. Conditions/callback exceptions propagate after prior side effects; no default invocation/caller completeness inferred.

facts.meaning: Partner registration normalizes TrainerType, cancels vehicles, loads trainer, triggers on_trainer_load with that actual trainer, then sequentially replaces each party owner and recalculates stats. Only after this loop does it commit PokemonGlobal.partner as type/name/trainer.id/trainer.party. Deregistration assigns nil.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: A missing trainer may be passed to subscribers; later trainer.party can fail. A callback or per-Pokemon failure occurs before final partner assignment but can retain vehicle/callback/earlier Pokemon owner/stat mutations. This is one concrete real receiver chain, not all wild/trainer/battle event producers.

facts.meaning: pbLoadTrainer validates existence of TrainerType via try_get, normalizes the type, queries the Trainer composite ID and returns data.to_trainer or nil. This method itself does not trigger on_trainer_load.
facts.premises_failure_cancel_partial_and_open: Specific battle/debug/partner callers decide whether and when to trigger. BattleStarting lines552/567/585, Debug_MenuCommands455/466 and WildEncounters447/456/460 were only located lexically by this receiver and remain OPEN here.

received_complete_semantic_payload.common_premise: Fixed built-in definitions and registration order, valid standard objects except named negative cases; no extra plugins/redefinitions/concurrent mutation; no behavior execution. Receiver must independently read adopted complete facts and actual own caller contexts.

facts.meaning: Species uses symbol-only registration: instantiate then assign by hash id, no secondary numeric ID. exists? maps a supplied Species to its id; get/try_get return a supplied Species instance unchanged, including an unregistered instance; String becomes symbol without case normalization; invalid argument kinds fail validation. get raises for absent key while try_get(nil) returns nil.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: Symbol family numeric IDs are not accepted. Stale external Species instances need not match current registry after load/redefinition. All concrete Pokemon species= / form= consumers remain own CRE responsibility.

facts.meaning: Nil or false species/form returns nil before validation. Otherwise species accepts Symbol, String or Species; form must be Integer. A Species argument contributes its base species, String becomes symbol; trial is <species>_<integer>. If DATA[trial] is nil, fall back to base key; return selected stored value only if selected key exists.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: Form0 still probes a _0 key. Negative integer is not independently rejected here. Missing base and form yields nil; no form cloning/registration or nearest-form search occurs. A form-specific hit can succeed independently of base presence under direct registry mutation.

facts.meaning: Every constructor assignment is listed in field_defaults. The constructor ordinarily retains supplied arrays/hashes by reference and floors only registered main-stat base values and EVs. Empty arrays/hashes and numeric0 are truthy and are retained, not replaced by defaults.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: The constructor is not the PBS parser: it does not validate all types/enumerations/ranges. A malformed base-stats object can fail before later fields initialize; supplied base/EV hashes can already have been mutated. Extra stat keys are retained. These defaults are not all actual PBS records.

facts.meaning: PBS validation maps six base-stat positions using Stat.pbs_order; maps repeated EV pairs into keyed values with later duplicate key wins; converts authored height/weight to rounded tenths with minimum1; checks required evolution parameter before marking evo[3]=false; removes duplicate/nil types in place.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: Direct constructor inputs bypass these preprocessing steps. Failure can preserve prior edits to the current data hash, and previously registered records remain in DATA. All raw species/form PBS bodies remain unreceived in this contribution.

facts.meaning: After ordinary species registration, final validation resolves offspring IDs and evolution targets/parameters against the registry. Evolution parameter nil type is forced nil, Integer is parsed nonnegative, non-String enum is resolved; String remains text. It builds one first encountered predecessor tuple per target and appends its shallow clone to each matching species, then replaces four species text baseline buckets.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: First is GameData::Species.each registration/insertion order and each evolution list order, not lowest species number or a uniqueness proof. Later references can fail after earlier field mutations; save occurs only after final validation returns. No cycle/collision-free family proof is inferred.

facts.meaning: Dedicated forms do not clear Species DATA. Form section identity is parsed as existing base species plus integer form, normalized to <species>_<form>, and checked for missing base/duplicate compound key before form registration. Each successful section registers before final all-form validation and final save.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: A later form or final validation failure retains earlier registered forms and base records; no rollback. The base species compiler has already run on the normal compile driver path. Direct calls and dynamic mutations require their own premises.

facts.meaning: Only when each property is nil, inherit base real_name, real_category, real_pokedex_entry, base_exp, growth_rate, gender_ratio, catch_rate, happiness, hatch_steps, incense, height, weight, color, shape, habitat and generation. These scalar/list-independent assignments use the base object value directly.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: False is not nil at this inheritance gate, although constructor || defaults can later replace false. real_form_name, pokedex_form and mega fields are not in this inheritance list. No deep immutable-value guarantee is introduced.

facts.meaning: Only when nil, types, base_stats, evs, tutor_moves, egg_moves, abilities, hidden_abilities, egg_groups, offspring and flags each receive one shallow clone of the corresponding base container.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: Explicit nonnil empty containers do not trigger that branch; generic file parser may already have changed an empty parsed array to nil. Nested elements are not recursively cloned. Constructor subsequently fills/floors main stats on the cloned or authored hash.

facts.meaning: When moves is not an Array or has length0, it retains/creates its outer target via ||= and pushes a clone of each base level/move pair.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: For normal parsed nil/empty arrays, outer and each pair are distinct from base. This is not a recursive deep clone. A truthy non-Array malformed direct value is not repaired by ||= and may fail on push after preceding inherited assignments.

facts.meaning: When evolutions is not an Array or has length0, it retains/creates the target then pushes a clone of each base evolution tuple.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: This includes inherited reverse-predecessor flags already present on base at that stage; later final-form validation recomputes reverse entries. Nested parameter objects are shared unless later rewritten. A malformed non-Array truthy target can fail at push.

facts.meaning: The three wild-item arrays inherit shallow clones together only when all three authored hash properties are nil. If any one is nonnil, none of the three is inherited; remaining nil properties later get constructor empty arrays.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: This is a joint group gate, not independent per-rarity fallback. Parser empty-array-to-nil normalization occurs before it; direct constructor/direct validation inputs can differ. Wild encounter rarity/ability/item selection remains OPEN here.

facts.meaning: Final forms validate evolution parameters for all registered records, skipping enum conversion for parameters already not Strings. They ignore reverse tuples while building first general and form-specific predecessor maps. Each record prefers [species,base_form] over general species, deletes old reverse tuples, appends selected clone, and adds a None forward edge to base predecessor only if that predecessor has no forward target of the species. Form text buckets append.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: Order-sensitive first predecessor remains; base_form honors first matching DefaultForm_N flag or own form. Earlier species/evolution mutations persist after a later failure. No guarantee of one connected acyclic lineage, runtime evolution eligibility or cache refresh follows.

facts.meaning: get_previous_species selects first evo[3] tuple or own base species. get_baby_species likewise uses only first reverse tuple, optionally gates that step by predecessor incense matching either parent item, then recurses when species changed. get_egg_moves returns nonempty own list, otherwise recursively asks predecessor matching the current form with get_species_form fallback.
facts.specific_premises_failure_and_open: No visited-set/cycle guard exists in these methods. Absent referenced records can raise or nil-method fail. Their returned lists may be stored lists rather than fresh copies. Complete breeding/evolution callers and actual species data lineage remain OPEN.

facts.meaning: Kernel.validate is private. Its sole argument must be a Hash; otherwise it raises ArgumentError before iterating. Conditions that are Arrays accept when any listed class/module satisfies value.is_a?. A Symbol condition checks value.respond_to?(symbol). Other conditions are given to value.is_a?.
facts.failure_and_limits: Class/module validation admits subclasses and is not coercion, bounds checking, nested-field validation or method-arity validation. facts.meaning: For supported conditions it traverses all Hash entries, builds failure strings, compacts nonfailures and returns nil if none remain; otherwise raises one ArgumentError combining the errors with CRLF.
facts.failure_and_limits: Successful checks do not replace or normalize values. A caller Hash has already been constructed before validate; equal Hash keys can collapse at that construction, so this API cannot promise preserving a caller conceptual list of repeated equal-value checks. No rollback of prior caller writes.
